caption:
Who does better in HYROX: the runner or the bodybuilder?

A study of 39,696 PRO and ELITE race results puts running near the center of the answer. A separate 11-person simulation linked better aerobic capacity and more endurance training with faster finishes. Strength stations still matter.

Our pick: the runner who has trained the stations. A big engine needs enough station-specific strength to keep moving. These studies did not directly race runners against bodybuilders.

Which athlete are you backing—and which station would change your mind?

caption:
What’s the big deal with bicarb—and why are elites using it?

It is a buffer, not a carb. The appeal is a possible edge when the effort gets very hard. The catch: benefits depend on the event and protocol, and your gut may object.

Continuous-running evidence is mixed: a review found a negligible adjusted average benefit, while a newer small 10K trial reported an improvement. A separate running trial found better gut tolerance with hydrogel but no faster 800 m.

Would you chase the marginal gain—or keep your race-day routine simple?
